awd_titl_txt: Travel: Student Travel Grant for ACM Special Interest Group on Data Communication Conference (SIGCOMM 2025)
awd_abstract_narration:
The 2025 ACM SIGCOMM Conference will be held in Coimbra, Portugal on September 8 - 11, 2025. This will be the 39th edition of the conference series.  Each year, the conference attracts hundreds of submissions, with acceptance rates typically in the ranging of 10-20%, underscoring its reputation as one of the most competitive venues in the field. The program committee, composed of leading experts from academia and industry, ensures that only the most significant and impactful works are presented. 

This project supports students from US universities to attend 2025 ACM SIGCOMM in person. Students will have the opportunity to present their work and be exposed to state-of-the-art developments in the field. They will also have the opportunity to interact with peers from institutions worldwide, meet with senior researchers, and participate in discussions that are likely to shape the future of the field. This grant will target graduate students who will substantially benefit from attending this conference but have limited travel funds. Priority will be given to first-time attendees.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.
org_dir_long_name: Directorate for Computer and Information Science and Engineering

por.por_cntn:
This award supported travel for graduate students from U.S. institutions to attend the ACM SIGCOMM 2025 conference, the leading international venue for research in computer networking and communications. Modern society relies on computer networks for nearly every aspect of daily life, including healthcare, education, transportation, agriculture, emergency response, scientific discovery, and access to information. Advances presented at SIGCOMM help improve the performance, security, reliability, and sustainability of these critical systems.

The primary outcome of this award was the professional development of the next generation of networking researchers and engineers. Travel support enabled students to participate in technical presentations, poster sessions, workshops, demonstrations, and mentoring activities that would otherwise have been inaccessible due to financial constraints. Through these activities, students gained first-hand exposure to cutting-edge research on topics such as artificial intelligence for networking, cloud and edge computing, wireless systems, Internet infrastructure, network security, and data-center technologies.

The award strengthened the U.S. research workforce by allowing students to interact directly with leading scientists and engineers from academia, industry, and government laboratories. These interactions helped students refine their research directions, establish professional networks, identify future collaborators, and explore career opportunities. Exposure to diverse research approaches and real-world challenges accelerated their technical growth and increased their ability to contribute to future innovations in networking and computing systems.

The benefits extended beyond the individual participants. Students returned to their home institutions with new technical knowledge, research ideas, and professional connections. They shared these experiences with fellow students, faculty mentors, and research groups, amplifying the impact of the award and promoting the dissemination of new scientific advances throughout the broader academic community.

The project contributed to the development of a highly skilled and diverse workforce capable of addressing future challenges in computer networking. By supporting student participation in SIGCOMM 2025, the award helped strengthen the research ecosystem that underpins the communication technologies essential to modern society.
